title: Convert Pod to Deployment
description: Convert a single Pod into a reliable 3-replica Deployment with hardened container security context and save the manifest.

environmentConstraints: Work only on the instance ckad9043.
No real cluster, container or SSH connection is used in this simulator.
The source Pod manifest is pre-created at /opt/course/9/holy-api-pod.yaml.

commands.purpose: Connect to the practice instance.
Inspect the raw Pod template to reuse its container spec.
commands.expectedStdout:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: holy-api
  namespace: pluto
  labels:
    app: holy-api
spec:
  containers:
  - name: holy-api
    image: httpd:2.4.41-alpine
    ports:
    - containerPort: 80

commands.exact: kubectl get pod holy-api -n pluto -o yaml --export
commands.purpose: Optionally inspect the live Pod configuration as a source for the Deployment template.
commands.expectedStdout:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: holy-api
  namespace: pluto
spec:
  containers:
  - name: holy-api
    image: httpd:2.4.41-alpine

commands.exact: kubectl create deployment holy-api --image=httpd:2.4.41-alpine -n pluto --dry-run=client -o yaml > /opt/course/9/holy-api-deployment.yaml
commands.purpose: Generate a starting Deployment manifest under the required path.
Edit the manifest to set replicas, labels, selector, and container security context.
Create the Deployment in Namespace pluto.
Delete the original single Pod once the Deployment is running.

artifacts.description: Final Deployment manifest saved on ckad9043.
artifacts.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: holy-api
  namespace: pluto
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: holy-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: holy-api
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: holy-api
        image: httpd:2.4.41-alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          privileged: false

successCriteria: A Deployment named holy-api exists in Namespace pluto with 3 replicas.
The Deployment pods use the container image from the original Pod.
The container securityContext sets allowPrivilegeEscalation: false and privileged: false.
The final manifest is saved at /opt/course/9/holy-api-deployment.yaml.
The original standalone Pod named holy-api no longer exists in Namespace pluto.
rationale: A Deployment manages ReplicaSets which in turn manage Pods, giving declarative replicas and self-healing. The Pod template's labels must match the Deployment selector, and container-level securityContext fields constrain privilege escalation and privileged mode.
referenceNotes: Deployment selectors are immutable; the Pod template labels must satisfy matchLabels.
Use kubectl create deployment --dry-run=client -o yaml to bootstrap a manifest quickly.
Deleting the original Pod after the Deployment owns labeled Pods avoids name conflicts and downtime.

title: ClusterIP Service and Curl Test
description: Create a labeled Pod and ClusterIP Service with port redirection, then verify access and logs from a temporary Pod.

environmentConstraints: Work only on the instance ckad9043.
No real cluster, container or SSH connection is used in this simulator.
Write the response and log files under /opt/course/10 on ckad9043.

commands.purpose: Connect to the practice instance.
Create the labeled nginx Pod targeted by the Service.
Create the internal Service redirecting TCP port 3333 to container port 80.

commands.purpose: Request the Service from a temporary Pod and save the HTML response.
Save the nginx access logs showing the incoming request.

commands.exact: kubectl get svc project-plt-6cc-svc -n pluto -o wide
commands.purpose: Confirm the Service is ClusterIP with the expected port mapping.
commands.expectedStdout:
NAME                   TYPE        CLUSTER-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)    AGE   SELECTOR
project-plt-6cc-svc    ClusterIP   10.96.145.22    <none>        3333/TCP   1m    project=plt-6cc-api

nginx Pod logs containing the request from the temporary Pod.

successCriteria: Pod project-plt-6cc-api exists in pluto with image nginx:1.17.3-alpine and label project=plt-6cc-api.
ClusterIP Service project-plt-6cc-svc exists in pluto selecting that Pod.

The Pod logs are saved in /opt/course/10/service_test.log and show the request.
rationale: A ClusterIP Service provides a stable in-cluster virtual IP and DNS name. Its selector matches Pod labels, and port/targetPort translate the Service port to the container port; endpoint wiring can be verified with curl from another Pod.
referenceNotes: Service selectors match Pod labels, not Deployment names.
ClusterIP is the default Service type and is only reachable inside the cluster.
Ephemeral Pods with --rm are useful for in-cluster connectivity tests.

title: PV, PVC and Volume Mount Deployment
description: Create a hostPath PersistentVolume, a matching PVC in earth, and a Deployment that mounts the claim.

environmentConstraints: Work only on the instance ckad9043.
No real cluster, container or SSH connection is used in this simulator.
Do not set storageClassName on either the PV or the PVC.

commands.purpose: Connect to the practice instance.

commands.exact:
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: earth-project-earthflower-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 2Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  hostPath:
    path: /Volumes/Data
EOF
commands.purpose: Create the 2Gi ReadWriteOnce hostPath PersistentVolume with no storage class.

commands.exact:
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: earth-project-earthflower-pvc
  namespace: earth
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 2Gi
  storageClassName: ""
EOF
commands.purpose: Create the PVC in earth requesting 2Gi without a storage class.
Confirm the PV is Bound to the claim.
commands.expectedStdout:
NAME                          CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   RECLAIM POLICY   STATUS   CLAIM                                      STORAGECLASS   REASON   AGE
earth-project-earthflower-pv   2Gi        RWO            Retain           Bound    earth/earth-project-earthflower-pvc                                   1m

commands.exact:
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: project-earthflower
  namespace: earth
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: project-earthflower
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: project-earthflower
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: httpd
        image: httpd:2.4.41-alpine
        volumeMounts:
        - name: project-data
          mountPath: /tmp/project-data
      volumes:
      - name: project-data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: earth-project-earthflower-pvc
EOF
commands.purpose: Create the Deployment that mounts the PVC at /tmp/project-data.
Verify the pod schedule and volume mount details.
commands.expectedStdout:
Name:         project-earthflower-6d7f8c9b4-x2mnp
Namespace:    earth
Mounts:
  /tmp/project-data from project-data (rw)

successCriteria: A PV named earth-project-earthflower-pv exists with 2Gi capacity, ReadWriteOnce, hostPath /Volumes/Data, and no storageClassName.
A PVC named earth-project-earthflower-pvc exists in earth requesting 2Gi ReadWriteOnce with no storage class and is Bound.
A Deployment named project-earthflower exists in earth using image httpd:2.4.41-alpine.
The Deployment pods mount the PVC at /tmp/project-data.
rationale: Static provisioning binds a PVC to a PV when capacity, access modes, and storageClassName match. Setting storageClassName: "" disables dynamic provisioning so the claim can bind to a classless PV; pods consume storage through a volume referencing the PVC and a container volumeMount.
referenceNotes: PersistentVolumes are cluster-scoped; PersistentVolumeClaims are namespaced.
An omitted storageClassName on a PV means the PV has no class and can satisfy classless claims.
A volumeMount mountPath must be an absolute path inside the container.

title: StorageClass with Retain Policy
description: Create a custom StorageClass with Retain reclaim policy, a pending PVC using it, and capture the provisioning failure reason.

environmentConstraints: Work only on the instance ckad9043.
No real cluster, container or SSH connection is used in this simulator.
The moon-retainer provisioner does not exist yet, so the PVC is expected to remain Pending.

commands.purpose: Connect to the practice instance.

commands.exact:
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: moon-retain
provisioner: moon-retainer
reclaimPolicy: Retain
EOF
commands.purpose: Create the StorageClass using the custom provisioner and Retain policy.

commands.exact:
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: moon-pvc-126
  namespace: moon
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 3Gi
  storageClassName: moon-retain
EOF
commands.purpose: Create the 3Gi PVC in moon using the new StorageClass.
Inspect the PVC events to find the provisioning failure message.
commands.expectedStdout:
Name:          moon-pvc-126
Namespace:     moon
Status:        Pending
Capacity:
Access Modes:  [ReadWriteOnce]
StorageClass:  moon-retain
Events:
  Type     Reason              Age   From                         Message
  -------  ------              ----  ----                         -------
  Warning  ProvisioningFailed  10s   persistentvolume-controller  no volume plugin matched name: moon-retainer

commands.purpose: Save the provisioning failure message from the PVC status into the required file.
Verify the StorageClass provisioner and reclaim policy.
commands.expectedStdout:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: moon-retain
provisioner: moon-retainer
reclaimPolicy: Retain

artifacts.description: Provisioning failure message extracted from the PVC status.
artifacts.content: no volume plugin matched name: moon-retainer

successCriteria: A StorageClass named moon-retain exists with provisioner moon-retainer and reclaimPolicy Retain.
A PVC named moon-pvc-126 exists in moon requesting 3Gi ReadWriteOnce with storageClassName moon-retain.
The PVC is Pending because the provisioner is unavailable.
The provisioning failure message is saved in /opt/course/13/pvc-126-reason.
rationale: A StorageClass names a provisioner used for dynamic volume provisioning. When the referenced provisioner is unavailable, the PVC stays Pending with a ProvisioningFailed event; reclaimPolicy Retain keeps the underlying volume after the PVC is deleted.
referenceNotes: StorageClasses are cluster-scoped and immutable in most fields, including provisioner and parameters.
reclaimPolicy on a StorageClass defaults to Delete when omitted.
Use kubectl describe pvc to see events explaining why provisioning failed.

kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secret-handler
  namespace: moon
spec:
  containers:
  - name: secret-handler
    image: httpd:2.4.41-alpine
    env:
    - name: SECRET1_USER
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: secret1
          key: user
    - name: SECRET1_PASS
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:

          key: pass

successCriteria: Secret secret1 exists in moon with keys user=test and pass=pwd.
Secret secret2 from the provided manifest exists in moon.
Pod secret-handler uses secretKeyRef to expose secret1 keys as SECRET1_USER and SECRET1_PASS.
Pod secret-handler mounts secret2 at /tmp/secret2.
The updated Pod manifest is saved at /opt/course/14/secret-handler-new.yaml.
rationale: Secrets are namespaced objects consumed by pods either as environment variables via secretKeyRef or as projected files through a secret volume. Env vars are read at container start, while mounted Secret volumes update automatically when the Secret changes.
referenceNotes: secretKeyRef.key refers to the key in the Secret's data/stringData map, not the Secret name.
A Secret volume creates one file per key at the mountPath.
Secrets are base64-encoded in data; stringData accepts plain text on creation.

title: ConfigMap for nginx HTML
description: Create a ConfigMap from an HTML file so the preconfigured nginx Deployment can serve it, then verify with a temporary Pod.

environmentConstraints: Work only on the instance ckad9043.
No real cluster, container or SSH connection is used in this simulator.
The web-moon Deployment is already configured to consume the ConfigMap.

commands.purpose: Connect to the practice instance.
Inspect the HTML content that must be stored in the ConfigMap.

commands.exact: kubectl get deploy web-moon -n moon -o yaml
commands.purpose: Check how the Deployment mounts the expected ConfigMap.
commands.expectedStdout:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-moon
  namespace: moon
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:alpine
        volumeMounts:
        - name: html
          mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
      volumes:
      - name: html
        configMap:
          name: configmap-web-moon-html

commands.purpose: Create the ConfigMap in moon with the file content under the index.html key.

commands.exact: kubectl run tmp-nginx -n moon --image=nginx:alpine --rm -it --restart=Never -- curl -s web-moon:80
commands.purpose: Verify nginx serves the ConfigMap content from a temporary Pod.

verificationCommands: kubectl run tmp-nginx -n moon --image=nginx:alpine --rm -it --restart=Never -- curl -s web-moon

successCriteria: A ConfigMap named configmap-web-moon-html exists in Namespace moon.
The ConfigMap has exactly the data key index.html with the content of /opt/course/15/web-moon.html.
The web-moon Deployment serves this content through its existing ConfigMap volume.
A curl test from a temporary nginx:alpine Pod returns the HTML content.
rationale: A ConfigMap stores non-sensitive configuration as key-value data. Mounting it as a volume projects each key as a file, which lets the nginx Deployment serve index.html without rebuilding the image; changing the ConfigMap updates the projected file.
referenceNotes: Use --from-file=KEY=PATH to control the ConfigMap data key name.
ConfigMap volume updates are eventually reflected in mounted files via a symlink swap.
ConfigMaps are namespaced, so the ConfigMap and Deployment must be in the same namespace.
